messages:
alex: quick follow-up from today's all-hands Q&A 1 want to capture the hiring/structure bits we discussed
tasha: thanks alex. short summary: no broad hiring freeze; were re-prioritizing headcount to mission-critical paths (runtime, customer reliability, Dedicated capacity). details/questions below.
ben: first question from Eng: will product-facing SEs be moved under Sales or stay with Product?
tasha: SEs supporting strategic accounts will report into a single GTM lead for consistency on customer promises. day-to-day work will stay tightly coordinated with Product Managers and Solutions Eng. intent is clearer ownership, not a functional split in collaboration.
alex: what's the expected timeline for moving people and org charts?
tasha: org mapping v1 goes out tomorrow. we expect most reporting changes to be effective at the start of next pay period (two weeks). individual managers will get mapping lists today.
mike: about headcount: any caps per team? managers asking if open reqs will be cancelled.
tasha: open reqs that map to prioritized pillars stay funded. noncritical roles will be frozen pending Q3 budget review. recruiting will contact hiring managers with status on each req by EOD.
sophia: internal mobility question: can ICs apply for jobs cross-functionally without manager sign-off during the window?	
ben: curious about performance calibration if someone moves teams mid-cycle.
people-bot: Internal Mobility window: Mar 15Mar 19. Submit interest via the portal: https://intranet.redwood.com/mobility :link:
tasha: mobility window open Mar 15Mar 19. We ask candidates to give a heads-up to their manager; formal sign-off isnt required to apply, but managers will be looped into interview scheduling.
alex: how are backfills fast-tracked if someone leaves a critical role to move internally?
tasha: submit a "critical-backfill" note to #hq-hiring. reviewers will gate based on customer impact and incident risk. short approvals aim for 72 hours.
mike: will there be role regrades or leveling changes for people who take on broader responsibilities post-shift?
tasha: yes, leveling reviews will run in two batches: immediate regrades for materially changed roles; standard ladder calibrations in next quarter. people can file regrade requests via the usual form and mark them as "reorg-impacted".
sophia: any change to the promotion/career path for engineers who move into customer-facing roles?	
ben: also wondering about equity/comp adjustments for lateral moves.
tasha: comp philosophy doesn't change. lateral moves keep base comp; substantial scope increases will be reviewed for compensation adjustments. promotions follow existing calibration practices.
alex: can managers hire contractors while reqs are frozen?
people-bot: Contractors: https://intranet.redwood.com/fin/contractors-policy :link:
tasha: short answer: contractor hires for critical delivery are allowed with finance sign-off. strategic long-term contractor spend needs exec approval.
mike: will on-call/responsibility shifting cause increased rotation frequency? some teams are already stretched.
tasha: we're not increasing rotation frequency globally. we'll rebalance on-call rosters to surface expertise where needed and add temporary coverage if load increases by >20%.
sophia: who should I contact about a specific mapping question for my team?
tasha: start with your manager. if unresolved, email people-ops@redwood with subject "mapping-escalation" and include role and proposed team.
alex: appreciate the clarity. i'll paste these notes into the follow-up doc and tag any open items.
people-bot: Summary doc: https://intranet.redwood.com/all-hands/mar14-reorg-summary :link: :memo:
